titleEn: How Long Does a Bathroom Renovation Take in Vancouver? A Realistic 2026 Timeline
titleZh: 温哥华浴室翻新需要多长时间？2026年真实工期指南
excerptEn: A bathroom renovation in Vancouver takes 3 weeks for cosmetic work, 6–10 weeks for a mid-range renovation, and 10–16 weeks for a full gut. This guide breaks down every phase with real Metro Vancouver timelines.
excerptZh: 温哥华的浴室翻新项目： cosmetics需3周，中档需6–10周，全拆重建需10–16周。本指南详细说明每个阶段的真实工期。
contentEn:
A typical bathroom renovation in Vancouver or Metro Vancouver takes anywhere from three weeks to four months, depending on the scope of work, the type of building, and how quickly the city processes your permits. This guide breaks down every phase with real timelines based on Reno Stars' 2024–2025 project data across Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and North Vancouver.

Planning a larger renovation? Reno Stars has renovated bathrooms across Metro Vancouver. Get a free, no-obligation quote.

How long does a bathroom renovation take in Vancouver? The short answer

Cosmetic bathroom refresh (paint, flooring, fixtures only, no plumbing changes): 2–3 weeks. Mid-range renovation (new vanity, tile, shower/tub replacement, some plumbing relocation): 6–10 weeks. Full gut renovation (structural changes, new layout, waterproofing, custom glass): 10–16 weeks.

Those numbers assume you are working with a contractor who has capacity to start within two weeks of signing. In 2025–2026, Metro Vancouver renovation timelines are longer than historical averages because contractor demand exceeds supply. Always add 1–2 weeks of buffer at the front end for quoting, contract negotiation, and deposit processing.

Detailed bathroom renovation timeline by phase

Phase 1: Planning and design (weeks 1–2 before demo)

Before any work begins, your contractor needs time to measure, specify materials, and submit accurate pricing. For mid-range and full gut projects, this phase typically runs 1–2 weeks:

  • Initial consultation and site measure: 1–2 visits
  • Material selections (tile, vanity, fixtures, hardware): 3–5 days for standard items; 6–10 weeks for custom-order pieces like curbless shower glass or imported tile
  • Written quote and contract: 3–7 days
  • Deposit and deposit clearing: 1–3 days

Custom glass shower enclosures and imported tile are common timeline killers. If you are specifying custom materials, order them before you sign the contract — lead times are not the contractor's problem to solve on your behalf.

Phase 2: Permits (if required, running concurrently)

Most bathroom renovations in Vancouver do not require a building permit. You need one when the scope includes:

  • Moving or adding plumbing drains or water supply lines (plumbing permit only: 4–8 weeks in Vancouver, 3–6 weeks in Burnaby/Surrey/Richmond)
  • Structural changes — removing or adding a wall, changing ceiling height, modifying a window opening
  • Any work in a strata property that affects common elements or requires a Form P or Form K approval
  • Waterproofing modifications in a building subject to the BC Building Code (new waterproofing for curbless showers in new construction requires engineering)

2026 update: Vancouver Building Department lead times have not fully recovered from the 2024–2025 permit backlog surge. Plan for the upper end of permit timelines, especially for structural work. A mid-range Vancouver bathroom with a plumbing permit alone typically runs 4–8 weeks from submission to approval.

Phase 3: Demo (1–3 days)

Demo for a single bathroom — removing tile, flooring, vanity, tub or shower, and any damaged drywall — runs one to three days. Condo demo requires strata coordination and may need a written scope submitted to the property manager 5–10 business days in advance. Strata noise and working-hour rules typically limit demo to weekdays between 9am and 5pm in condo buildings.

Phase 4: Rough-in plumbing and electrical (2–5 days)

This is the phase where things are most invisible and most important. Rough-in covers:

  • Drain and supply line relocation or new plumbing connections (if the layout is changing)
  • New electrical circuits for heated flooring, vanity lighting, or upgraded exhaust fans
  • Waterproofing inspection (required for all new shower enclosures in BC — a building inspector must verify membrane integrity before tile is installed)

Waterproofing inspections are a hard stop — no tile goes in until the inspection passes. If the inspector fails the membrane, remediation takes 1–3 additional days and a reinspection must be scheduled. In a condo, this also means the property manager's inspector may need to attend, adding scheduling complexity.

Phase 5: Tiling and finishing (5–12 days)

Tile work is typically the longest single phase in a Vancouver bathroom renovation:

  • Backer board installation and seam sealing: 1 day
  • Waterproof membrane application: 1 day (flood testing 24 hours later if required)
  • Floor tile installation: 1–2 days
  • Wall tile installation: 2–4 days (more for curbless showers with large format tile)
  • Grout and seal: 1–2 days (grout needs 24–48 hours before it can be sealed)
  • Caulking and final seal: 1 day

Curbless (walk-in) showers require more careful waterproofing and slightly longer tile phases than standard tub or neo-angle shower conversions. If you are specifying large-format tile (24" × 48" or larger), budget an extra day for layout and cutting adjustments.

Phase 6: Vanity, fixtures, and glass (2–5 days of installation, plus delivery)

After tile and grout cure, the final install phase covers:

  • Vanity and countertop (custom countertops typically require a template visit, then 10–14 days to fabricate and install)
  • Faucet, shower head, bath hardware: 1 day
  • Mirror and lighting fixtures: half day
  • Toilet (if replaced, not reused): half day
  • Glass shower enclosure or curbless glass panel install: 1 day (often a separate trade, scheduled separately)
  • Exhaust fan connection and testing: half day

Custom glass enclosures — frameless or heavy glass — typically require a site measure after tile is complete, then 2–3 weeks to fabricate. This is the most commonly underestimated lead time in Vancouver bathroom renovations. Order your glass early.

Phase 7: Final inspection and punch list (1–3 days)

For renovations requiring a plumbing permit, a final plumbing inspection must be passed before the space can be used. The contractor completes a punch list (minor adjustments, caulking touch-ups, fixture leveling), then schedules the inspection. Inspectors in Vancouver typically visit within 3–5 business days of the call. A failed inspection adds 1–3 days minimum.

Timeline by bathroom renovation type in Vancouver

Renovation typeScopeTypical durationPermit needed?
Cosmetic refreshPaint, new flooring, new fixtures, no plumbing changes2–3 weeksNo (condo bylaw review only)
Mid-range updateNew vanity, tub/tile refresh, new faucet, exhaust fan6–10 weeksPlumbing permit if moving any plumbing
Full gut renovationNew layout, new shower, new waterproofing, new glass10–16 weeksYes (plumbing + possibly structural)
Strata condo bathroomAny of the above, but in a condo buildingAdd 1–3 weeks for strata approvalsAlways check strata bylaws first

Vancouver bathroom renovation timeline: realistic vs optimistic

Contractors quote timelines based on ideal conditions. Reality adds:

  • Material delivery delays (custom tile from Italy or Spain: 8–14 weeks, sometimes longer)
  • City inspection scheduling (Vancouver building inspectors: 3–7 business days for non-emergency visits)
  • Strata board approvals in condo buildings (allow 5–15 business days for Form K/P processing)
  • Backordered fixtures (heated floor systems, smart toilets, designer faucets: 4–10 weeks in 2025–2026)
  • Undiscovered structural issues once demo opens the wall (rot, old wiring, improper prior work)

Reno Stars communicates material lead times before you sign, not after. We track custom-order timelines at the contract stage so surprises don't extend your renovation by weeks.

Real Vancouver and Metro Vancouver bathroom renovation examples

These are completed projects with verified timelines:

Master bathroom, Vancouver (Kensington neighbourhood): Full gut, new curbless shower, double vanity, heated floor, frameless glass. Scope included moving the toilet drain 18 inches. Timeline: 12 weeks (includes 2-week strata approval at the beginning). View this project →

Daughter's bath, Richmond ( Richmond neighbourhood): Mid-range update, new tub replaced with neo-angle shower, new tile surround, new vanity, new exhaust fan. No layout change. Timeline: 7 weeks. View this project →

Two-bathroom renovation, Burnaby (Brentwood neighbourhood): Full gut on both bathrooms, shared wall demo, two waterproofing inspections, custom glass enclosures. Timeline: 14 weeks (includes custom glass lead time of 3 weeks). View this project →

How to keep your Vancouver bathroom renovation on schedule

  • Order custom materials before signing. Glass enclosures, imported tile, and custom vanities are the top timeline killers. Get lead times from your contractor before you commit to a start date.
  • Know your strata rules before demo. Condo residents: submit your renovation scope to the property manager before you sign. Most Vancouver and Burnaby condo buildings require reno applications 5–15 business days before work starts. Demo without strata approval can result in a stop-work order.
  • Fix moisture or mould before demo. If your bathroom has existing moisture damage, get a contractor assessment before demo begins. Remediation for mould or rot found behind tile can add $1,500–$8,000 and 1–2 weeks to your timeline.
  • Decide on smart fixtures early. Heated floor systems, smart toilets, and digital shower controls require electrical rough-in before tiling. These cannot be added after the fact without reopening the wall.
  • Build in a 2-week buffer. Even well-run Vancouver bathroom renovations encounter one unexpected issue: a hidden drain issue, a delayed inspection, a backordered part. Budgeting 14 days of contingency is standard practice for mid-range and full gut projects.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does a small bathroom renovation take in Vancouver?

A small (powder room or 3-piece compact) cosmetic or mid-range bathroom renovation in Vancouver typically runs 3–8 weeks from contract signing to final inspection. A full gut on a small bathroom runs 8–12 weeks because the same permit, inspection, and trade scheduling steps apply regardless of square footage.

How long does a condo bathroom renovation take in Vancouver?

A condo bathroom renovation in Vancouver requires strata approval before work begins, which adds 1–3 weeks in most buildings. Once approved, timelines match the types above. The key constraint in condo buildings is working hours: most Vancouver, Burnaby, and Richmond strata restrict reno work to weekdays 9am–5pm, which can slow demo and tile cutting phases by extending what would be a 1-day demo into 2–3 days.

Do I need a permit for a bathroom renovation in Vancouver?

You need a plumbing permit if you are moving any drain, supply line, or plumbing fixture location. You need a building permit if you are removing or adding a wall, modifying structural elements, or changing a window opening. Cosmetic refresh — paint, new flooring, new fixtures in the same locations — does not require a permit in most Vancouver and Metro Vancouver municipalities, but always check your building bylaws if you are in a strata property.

What is the longest phase in a Vancouver bathroom renovation?

Custom glass enclosure fabrication is typically the longest single lead time, running 2–3 weeks from site measure to delivery in 2025–2026. Waterproofing inspection also adds a hard 24-hour waiting period after membrane application before tiling can begin. Material ordering — especially for imported tile, custom vanity tops, or designer fixtures — is the most common source of unexpected delays.

Can I live in my home during a bathroom renovation in Vancouver?

Yes for single-bathroom homes with an alternative toilet — the kitchen or ensuite can serve as the temporary bathroom. For homes with only one bathroom, contractors typically ask homeowners to vacate for 3–5 days during the wet phases (waterproofing and tiling) when the bathroom is not functional. contentZh:
温哥华及大温哥华地区的浴室翻新项目通常需要三周到四个月不等，具体取决于工程范围、建筑类型以及城市处理许可证的速度。本指南基于 Reno Stars 2024–2025 年在温哥华、本拿比、列治文和北温哥华的项目数据，详细说明每个阶段的真实工期。

正在计划更大的翻新项目？Reno Stars 承接大温哥华地区的浴室翻新工程。获取免费、无义务的报价。

温哥华浴室翻新需要多长时间？简短答案

浴室 cosmetic 刷新工程（仅油漆、地板、 fixtures，不改管道）：2–3 周。中档翻新（新洗手台、瓷砖、淋浴/浴缸更换、部分管道重新定位）：6–10 周。全拆重建（结构变更、新布局、防水处理、定制玻璃）：10–16 周。

上述时间为您与有空闲档期的承包商签约后两周内开工的情况。2025–2026 年，大温哥华地区的承包商需求超过供给，工期普遍比历史平均更长。在报价、合同谈判和定金处理阶段，预留 1–2 周的缓冲 时间。

各阶段详细浴室翻新工期

第一阶段：规划和设计（动工前 1–2 周）

在任何工程开始前，您的承包商需要时间进行测量、确定材料规格并提交准确报价。对于中档和全拆重建项目，此阶段通常需要 1–2 周：

  • 初步 consultation 和现场测量：1–2 次拜访
  • 材料选择（瓷砖、洗手台、 fixtures、五金件）：标准项目 3–5 天；定制 order 产品（如无障碍淋浴玻璃或进口瓷砖）需 6–10 周
  • 书面报价和合同：3–7 天
  • 定金及定金到账：1–3 天

定制玻璃淋浴房和进口瓷砖是常见的工期杀手。如果您指定定制材料，请在签约前 order 它们——交期不是承包商需要为您解决的问题。

第二阶段：许可证（如需要，可同步进行）

温哥华大多数浴室翻新不需要 building permit。在以下情况下需要：

  • 移动或添加排水管或供水管路（仅 plumbing permit：温哥华 4–8 周，本拿比/素里/列治文 3–6 周）
  • 结构变更——拆除或添加墙体、更改天花板高度、修改窗户洞口
  • 任何影响公共区域或需要 Form P 或 Form K 审批的 strata 物业工程
  • BC 建筑规范所辖建筑的新防水修改（新建无障碍淋浴的防水处理需要 engineering）

2026 年更新：温哥华建筑部门的许可证处理时间尚未从 2024–2025 年的积压中完全恢复。规划许可证时间时，请按上限计算。温哥华带 plumbing permit 的中档浴室翻新，从提交到审批通常需要 4–8 周。

第三阶段：拆除（1–3 天）

单间浴室的拆除——移除瓷砖、地板、洗手台、浴缸或淋浴以及任何受损的干墙——需要一至三天。公寓拆除需要 strata 协调，可能需要在开工前 5–10 个工作日内向物业经理提交书面工程范围。Strata 噪音和工作时间规定通常将公寓拆除限制在周一至周五上午 9 点至下午 5 点之间。

第四阶段：管道和电气 rough-in（2–5 天）

这是最不可见但最重要的阶段。Rough-in 包括：

  • 排水管和供水管路的重新定位或新 plumbing 连接（如果布局变更）
  • 地板供暖、洗手台照明或升级排气扇的新电气线路
  • 防水 inspection（在 BC 所有新淋浴 enclosure 均需要——在瓷砖安装前，检查员必须验证 membrane 完整性）

防水 inspection 是硬性截止——在检查通过前不能安装瓷砖。如果检查员 membrane 不合格，修复需要额外的 1–3 天，并必须重新安排 inspection。在公寓中，这也意味着可能需要物业经理的检查员到场，增加了调度复杂性。

第五阶段：瓷砖和精加工（5–12 天）

瓷砖工程通常是温哥华浴室翻新中最耗时的单个阶段：

  • 背板安装和接缝密封：1 天
  • 防水 membrane 施工：1 天（如果需要，进行 24 小时 flood testing）
  • 地板瓷砖铺设：1–2 天
  • 墙砖铺设：2–4 天（大型瓷砖无障碍淋浴时间更长）
  • 填缝和密封：1–2 天（填缝需要 24–48 小时才能密封）
  • 收尾密封：1 天

无障碍（步入式）淋浴需要比标准浴缸或斜角淋浴改造更细致的防水处理，瓷砖阶段略长。如果您指定大规格瓷砖（24" × 48" 或更大），预算额外一天的布局和切割调整时间。

第六阶段：洗手台、 fixtures 和玻璃（安装 2–5 天，外加配送）

瓷砖和填缝固化后，最后安装阶段包括：

  • 洗手台和台面（定制台面通常需要模板 visit，然后需要 10–14 天制造和安装）
  • 水龙头、淋浴头、浴室五金件：1 天
  • 镜子和照明 fixtures：半天
  • 马桶（如果更换而非重复使用）：半天
  • 玻璃淋浴房或无障碍玻璃面板安装：1 天（通常是 separate trade，单独安排）
  • 排气扇连接和测试：半天

定制玻璃 enclosure——无框或重型玻璃——通常在瓷砖完工后需要现场测量，然后需要 2–3 周制造。这是温哥华浴室翻新中最容易被低估的 lead 时间。在瓷砖完成后立即 order 您的玻璃。

第七阶段：最终 inspection 和 punch list（1–3 天）

对于需要 plumbing permit 的翻新工程，必须通过最终 plumbing inspection 才能使用该空间。承包商完成 punch list（轻微调整、密封胶修整、 fixtures 调平），然后安排 inspection。温哥华的检查员通常在接到电话后 3–5 个工作日内 visit。不合格的 inspection 至少增加 1–3 天。

温哥华浴室翻新类型的工期对比

翻新类型范围典型工期需要许可证？
Cosmetic 刷新油漆、新地板、新 fixtures，不改 plumbing2–3 周否（公寓需查看 strata 法规）
中档翻新新洗手台、浴缸/瓷砖刷新、新水龙头、排气扇6–10 周移动 plumbing 时需要 plumbing permit
全拆重建新布局、新淋浴、新防水、新玻璃10–16 周是（plumbing + 可能需要结构）
Strata 公寓浴室上述任何类型，但在公寓建筑中另加 1–3 周 strata 审批开工前务必查看 strata 法规

温哥华浴室翻新工期：现实 vs 乐观估计

承包商按理想条件报价。现实会 adding：

  • 材料配送延迟（意大利或西班牙进口瓷砖：8–14 周，有时更长）
  • 城市 inspection 排程（温哥华建筑检查员：非紧急 visit 通常需要 3–7 个工作日）
  • Strata 董事会审批（公寓建筑：通常需要 5–15 个工作日处理 Form K/P）
  • Fixtures 缺货（地板供暖系统、智能马桶、设计师水龙头：2025–2026 年需 4–10 周）
  • 拆除后发现结构问题（腐烂、旧线路、不当 prior 工程）

Reno Stars 在签约前沟通材料 lead 时间，而不是之后。我们在整个合同阶段跟踪定制 order 时间表，这样惊喜不会延长您的翻新工期。

真实的大温哥华地区浴室翻新案例

以下是已完成的真实项目及其经验证的工期：

温哥华主浴室（Kensington 社区）：全拆重建，新无障碍淋浴、双洗手台、地板供暖、无框玻璃。工程范围包括将马桶排水管移动 18 英寸。工期：12 周（包含开头 2 周 strata 审批）。查看此项目 →

列治文女儿浴室（列治文社区）：中档翻新，新斜角淋浴替代浴缸、新瓷砖 surrounding、新洗手台、新排气扇。布局未变。工期：7 周。查看此项目 →

本拿比两浴室翻新（Brentwood 社区）：两间浴室全拆重建、共用墙拆除、两项防水 inspection、定制玻璃 enclosure。工期：14 周（包含 3 周定制玻璃 lead 时间）。查看此项目 →

如何确保温哥华浴室翻新按计划进行

  • 在签约前 order 定制材料。玻璃 enclosure、进口瓷砖和定制洗手台是最大的工期杀手。向您的承包商确认 lead 时间后再确定开工日期。
  • 在拆除前了解您的 strata 法规。公寓住户：在签约前向物业经理提交翻新范围。大多数温哥华和本拿比公寓楼要求在开工前 5–15 个工作日提交 renovation 申请。未获 strata 审批就开工可能导致 stop-work order。
  • 在拆除前处理潮湿或霉变。如果您的浴室已有潮湿损坏，请在开始拆除前获取承包商评估。发现瓷砖后面的霉变或腐烂进行修复可能需要额外 $1,500–$8,000 并增加 1–2 周工期。
  • 尽早决定智能 fixtures。地板供暖系统、智能马桶和数字淋浴控制器需要在瓷砖铺设前进行电气 rough-in。这些在事后无法添加——除非重新打开墙体。
  • 预留 2 周 buffer。即使是运行良好的温哥华浴室翻新项目也会遇到一个意外问题：隐藏的排水问题、延误的 inspection、缺货的零件。为中档和全拆重建项目预留 14 天的应急时间是标准做法。

常见问题

温哥华小浴室翻新需要多长时间？

温哥华小浴室（洗手间或三件套紧凑型）cosmetic 或中档翻新，从签约到最终 inspection 通常需要 3–8 周。全拆重建小浴室需要 8–12 周，因为无论建筑面积大小，相同的 permit、inspection 和 trade 排程步骤均适用。

温哥华公寓浴室翻新需要多长时间？

温哥华公寓浴室翻新需要在工程开始前获得 strata 审批，在大多数建筑中增加 1–3 周。获批后，工期与上述类型相同。公寓建筑中的关键限制是工作时间：大多数温哥华、本拿比和列治文 strata 将翻新工作限制在周一至周五上午 9 点至下午 5 点，这可能将本应 1 天的拆除延长至 2–3 天。

温哥华浴室翻新需要许可证吗？

如果您移动任何排水管、供水管路或 fixtures 位置，则需要 plumbing permit。如果您拆除或添加墙体、更改结构元素或修改窗户洞口，则需要 building permit。Cosmetic 刷新——油漆、新地板、在相同位置更换新 fixtures——在大多数温哥华和大温哥华 municipality 不需要许可证，但如果您在 strata 物业，请务必先查看您的建筑法规。

温哥华浴室翻新中最耗时的阶段是什么？

定制玻璃 enclosure 制造通常是最长的单个 lead 时间，2025–2026 年从现场测量到交付通常需要 2–3 周。防水 inspection 也在 membrane 施工后增加硬性 24 小时等待期，才能开始铺设瓷砖。材料 ordering——尤其是进口瓷砖、定制台面或设计师 fixtures——是意外延误的最常见原因。

在温哥华浴室翻新期间我可以住在家里吗？

对于有备用卫生间的单浴室住宅——厨房或主卧套间可以作为临时浴室，可以住在家里。对于只有一个卫生间的住宅，承包商通常要求住户在潮湿阶段（防水和瓷砖铺设）期间迁出 3–5 天，此时浴室无法使用。Reno Stars 协调排程，尽量减少浴室完全无法使用的天数。
